A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VideoChat-M1 and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary Sections A.1–A.6. All 21 pages of each version support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, inference-efficiency measurements, ablations, and qualitative examples in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark results, component ablations, and Appendix A.6 tool-reliance experiment.

M1.justification: The CPP generation, execution, communication, and answer-aggregation procedures and SFT/MARL objectives remain unchanged. Renaming Space Tool to Spatial Tool and correcting Figure 4's reference-model label do not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: The training datasets in Table 10 and eight evaluation benchmarks remain unchanged, covering the same long-video QA, video reasoning, spatial intelligence, and temporal-grounding tasks.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators in Tables 1–2, 5, and 11 and the qualitative comparisons remain the same. Added related-work citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A.6 retain the same metrics, data sizes, model configurations, frame-selection procedures, training budgets, and inference settings. Settings moved by text reflow are not newly introduced protocols.

E4.justification: The agent-count/diversity, reward/dropout, SFT/MARL, tuning, aggregation, and tool-reliance ablations are retained unchanged. Appendix CPP case studies and qualitative comparisons also test the same questions with the same evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No statistical reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: All tabulated values, plotted results, and qualitative outputs remain unchanged. Result reporting receives a limited correction: v2 deletes introductory claims assigning a 3.6% LongVideoBench gain to Gemini 1.5 Pro and a 2.4% VSIBench gain to InternVL-3-241B. Table 1 in both versions supports those margins against Gemini 2.5 Pro and InternVL-3.5-241B, respectively.

T1.justification: The policy equations, reward formulation, GRPO objective, and Appendix A.5 convergence discussion are unchanged. Removing manuscript-line references does not revise mathematical reasoning or add a proof.

C1.justification: The introduction drops the two specifically misattributed numerical superiority claims described under E6. The central CPP/MARL contributions, novelty assertions, eight-benchmark scope, and broad performance and parameter-efficiency claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning agent diversity, collaboration, dropout, efficiency, fault tolerance, convergence, and independence from specialized tools remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: Appendices A.1–A.3 and A.6 retain the same data construction, prompts, tool backbones, hyperparameters, hardware, LoRA configuration, and inference details. Tool renaming introduces no new reproducibility information or access instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to Low-resolution action recognition for tiny actions challenge, G-UBS, When top-ranked recommendations fail, and TimeSuite. It also softens the assertion that existing RL methods cannot co-train heterogeneous agents to saying they struggle to do so; the overall positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: The abstract and introductory/related-work paragraphs are condensed, with limited methodological prose editing. Other edits include Spatial Tool terminology, corresponding-author designations, funding acknowledgement, and removal of obsolete appendix line references; the section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves before the Introduction heading, Figure 2 is resized, and the main text reflows. Figure 3 updates tool labels, Figure 4 changes the KL-related label from Reward Model to Reference Model, and Table 11 updates its tool heading. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity and internal consistency by correcting Figure 4's reference-model label and removing introductory baseline attributions inconsistent with Table 1. Shorter exposition also improves presentation. These are limited gains: the methods, experimental evidence, and theoretical support remain unchanged.
